The Colour Rendering Index (CRI) measures how accurately a light source reproduces colors compared to natural light (such as sunlight or incandescent light).  
Incandescent lamps produce light by heating a filament, emitting a continuous spectrum similar to blackbody radiation, which results in very accurate color rendering. They typically have a CRI close to 100.  
LEDs can have high CRI values (some >90), but standard ones may vary.  
Fluorescent lamps often have CRI values in the 60–90 range depending on type.  
High pressure sodium vapour lamps have very poor CRI (around 20–30).  

Thus, among the options, incandescent lamps have the highest CRI.
